known_shas_note: Every heartbeat.sh body this package has ever PUBLISHED, newest first, including the current one. PREPEND to this list when re-vendoring - never rewrite it, and never drop an entry. The `update` subcommand (src/update.js planScriptRefresh) uses it to tell an older copy of OURS, which it refreshes, from an edit the CUSTOMER made, which it never touches. Dropping a sha silently reclassifies every customer still on that version as having edited the file, and update then leaves them stale forever. Measured with `git show <tag>:src/assets/heartbeat.sh | sha256sum`: 18fbd977 shipped in v2.7.0 (the first release carrying the asset at all), 8992ec0b in v2.7.1, c3d8f14d in v2.11.0. (The verb in the first sentence said APPEND while the recipe below said PREPEND; the list is newest-first and src/setup.test.js asserts sha256 === known_shas[0], so PREPEND is the correct one and both now say it.)
why_byte_identical: This file is a VERBATIM copy of the origin path at the origin commit, deliberately unmodified - no header was added, because adding one would change the bytes and make a drift check against upstream impossible. Provenance lives here instead. Re-vendor with: cp <idea-base.us>/.claude/hooks/heartbeat.sh src/assets/heartbeat.sh && update sha256 + origin_commit above && PREPEND the new sha256 to known_shas. src/setup.test.js asserts the sha256 recorded here, which catches a local edit, and that sha256 is the first entry of known_shas; byte-identity with upstream is a cross-repo check neither repo's CI can perform today. For v2.11.0 that cross-repo check WAS performed by hand and is recorded here: `git show 4c842e5:.claude/hooks/heartbeat.sh | sha256sum` in idea-base.us returned c3d8f14d..., matching the sha256 above - verified against origin/main itself rather than against a local checkout, because a checkout can be stale and silently make a drift check pass.
